chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who catches the second rak'ah of the salat (prayer) with the Imam, while it is his first. What should he do when the Imam sits for the tashahhud? He said: He should sit lightly without settling himself fully in sitting. Then when it is the Imam’s third rak'ah and it is his second, he should remain briefly when the Imam rises, to the measure of what he would recite for the tashahhud, then he should catch up with the Imam.

He said: And I asked him about one who catches the last two rak'ahs of the salat (prayer): what should he do regarding recitation? He said: Recite in them, for they are your first two rak'ahs; and do not make the beginning of your salat (prayer) its end.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer being performed in congregation
key_terms.الْأُولَيَانِ: the first two rak'ahs as counted for the follower himself
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader being followed in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.لِلتَّشَهُّدِ: for the testimony recited while seated in salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: How should a person complete salat (prayer) if he joins the Imam in the second or last two rak'ahs?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the rulings for a follower who joins congregational salat (prayer) after missing one or two rak'ahs. It clarifies how he should sit during the Imam’s tashahhud and that the rak'ahs he personally begins with are treated as his first rak'ahs for purposes such as recitation. Its significance lies in detailing the proper order of actions for the latecomer in congregational prayer.
